The linked discussion says that contributor has a solution covering the related scaling, size, and safe-zone behavior, so an independent implementation design would duplicate ongoing work.

The current Peek code routes image dimensions through ImagePreviewer.GetPreviewSizeAsync, FilePreview.UpdatePreviewSizeAsync, and MainWindow.FilePreviewer_PreviewSizeChanged, where monitor scale, the 80% cap, minimums, and title-bar height interact.
The upstream timeline contains only automatic dedupe-digest cross-references; no implementation pull request is linked, and no prior MuyuanMS/PowerToys trace existed before this mirror.

issue_context.summary: Peek does not preserve a 512 x 512 image's native physical-pixel content size on non-100% scaled displays, with different incorrect results after a mixed-DPI monitor transition and image navigation.
known_information: The report was reproduced on a current-main 0.102 development build.
At 175% scaling, the reporter expected an approximately 512 x 596 outer-pixel window for a 512 x 512 image but observed 820 x 586.
After moving to a 125% display, the report records 583 x 417, then 583 x 563 after navigating away and back to the same image.
The expected behavior preserves image content at native physical-pixel size when it is within Peek's 80% monitor cap; window chrome may vary by display.

ImagePreviewer.GetPreviewSizeAsync returns the image size as PreviewSize.MonitorSize; FilePreview.UpdatePreviewSizeAsync raises PreviewSizeChanged; MainWindow.FilePreviewer_PreviewSizeChanged derives content and window sizes from monitor scale, monitor bounds, minimums, and TitleBarControl.ActualHeight.
The issue author is a repository collaborator and is assigned to this issue.
No diagnostic attachment was supplied, no implementation PR is linked, and no earlier MuyuanMS/PowerToys issue or pull-request trace referenced Issue 50244.
inferences: The reported dimensions are consistent with more than one interacting DPI-unit boundary, including content conversion, title-bar height, minimum sizing, and monitor selection; the report alone does not isolate one independently safe patch.
The assigned contributor's stated broader solution may intentionally coordinate this defect with the related cross-display and minimum-size work.
issue_context.analysis: The public report and source identify the full sizing pipeline, but the active owner has already scoped a connected solution. Producing an alternative root-cause claim or file-level patch plan now would risk contradicting or duplicating that work. This artifact therefore records the concrete evidence and ownership decision rather than presenting a speculative design as ready for approval.
initial_investigation: Retrieved the live issue body, comments, labels, assignee, and complete timeline; the timeline has no linked implementation, only automatic dedupe-digest references.
Reviewed live Issues 50193 and 50243. They remain open; Issue 50243 contains the assigned contributor's statement that a solution for several Peek scaling and size problems is forthcoming.
Inspected MainWindow.xaml.cs, FilePreview.xaml.cs, ImagePreviewer.cs, and WindowConstants.cs in local current main, plus the prior Peek image-scaling history change.
Searched MuyuanMS/PowerToys issues and pull requests for Issue 50244 traces; none existed. Fork mirror issue 612 now preserves the sanitized report and ownership decision.
